chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he used to say whenever the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared:
'O God! Enter it upon us with safety, and Islam, and certainty, and faith, and righteousness, and divine enablement for what You love and are pleased with.'

key_terms.البر: Righteousness, comprehensive piety encompassing good deeds
key_terms.التوفيق: Divine enablement, God's granting of success in good deeds — the belief that human action requires God's assistance
key_terms.السلامة: Safety, well-being, soundness — physical and spiritual
key_terms.اليقين: Certainty, firm conviction — the opposite of doubt

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Sadiq recite upon sighting the Ramadan crescent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) had a practice of reciting a specific supplication each time he witnessed the sighting of the new crescent moon marking the beginning of Ramadan. The supplication asks God to grant the arrival of Ramadan accompanied by six spiritual blessings: safety (salamah), Islam, certainty (yaqin), faith (iman), righteousness (birr), and divine enablement (tawfiq) for all that pleases God. This narration reflects the Shia Imam's practice of treating the sighting of Ramadan's crescent as a sacred moment requiring dedicated supplication, acknowledging that spiritual readiness for the month of fasting is itself a gift from God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> used to say whenever the crescent of the Month of Ramazan commenced:

‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Enter it upon us with the safety, and the conviction, and the faith, and the righteousness, and the inclination to whatever You<sup>azwj</sup> Love and whatever You<sup>azwj</sup> are Pleased with’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Am mar who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when looking at the crescent of the month of Ramadan would say, “
0 Allah, bring it (the month of Ramadan) upon us with peace and submission (to Your will), certainty, belief, virtue and good opportunity for whatever You love and consent with.’”
